sections.name: Databases and Data Engineering
sections.outcome: Design, build, query, evolve, and recover data systems that turn heterogeneous inputs into reliable structured, relational, analytical, nonrelational, and graph data products.
includes: Selecting representations, storage models, transformations, and operational guarantees from access, integrity, scale, and recovery requirements.
Integrating schema-governed records, databases, pipelines, and distributed data systems.
excludes: Statistical modeling or machine-learning training after data preparation.
Application behavior whose central challenge is not data storage, transformation, retrieval, or reliability.

sample_tasks.instruction: Turn a short list of customer facts into named, typed records suitable for storage.

Design one marketplace data platform that validates incoming partner records, stores and queries transactional data, builds recoverable analytical pipelines, maintains document and graph views, and meets stated migration, backup, partition, and consistency requirements.

sections.name: Schema-Governed Structured Data
sections.outcome: Interpret schemas, construct records from supplied or generated values, integrate heterogeneous documents, and serialize the resulting typed data correctly.
includes: Structural and value constraints, grounded extraction, permitted generation, and cross-document integration.
JSON, YAML, XML, and flattened CSV representations.
excludes: Designing persistent database schemas or indexes.
Scheduling recurring ingestion and transformation jobs.

sample_tasks.instruction: Represent three stated attributes as a typed record with the requested field names.

Using one regulatory filing and its tables, construct a schema-valid nested dataset, distinguish extracted from explicitly generated values, reconcile repeated entities, and serialize the same dataset as JSON, YAML, XML, and flattened CSV.

sections.name: Schema-Governed Record Construction
sections.outcome: Apply structural and scalar constraints while constructing valid records from supported facts or explicitly authorized generated values.
includes: Required and optional fields, types, enums, bounds, patterns, nullability, arrays, and nested objects.
Separating source-grounded extraction from value generation.
excludes: Format-specific escaping and markup syntax.
Relational table and index design.

sample_tasks.instruction: Read a small object schema and determine which candidate record satisfies its required fields, types, and allowed values.
For one nested permit schema and partially specified application, audit every constraint, map all supported facts, and generate only the missing values the request explicitly authorizes.

sections.name: Schema Constraint Interpretation
sections.outcome: Determine whether record shapes and values satisfy explicit structural, scalar, and collection constraints.
includes: Required properties, additional-property rules, nested cardinality, arrays, and nullable fields.
Type, enum, range, pattern, and date-time constraints.
excludes: Inferring facts from narrative documents.
Choosing storage schemas or engines.

sample_tasks.instruction: For a schema with one required integer and one optional string, identify which candidate records have permitted shapes and types.
Audit a nested record against required-field, additional-property, type, enum, numeric-bound, pattern, date-time, array-cardinality, and nullability constraints, reporting every violation.

sections.name: Grounded Record Mapping
sections.outcome: Map explicitly supported facts from prose or simple tables into the correct fields of a constrained schema without inventing unsupported values.
includes: Entity, quantity, date, status, classification, and contact-field extraction.
Type conversion and schema-permitted omission or null handling.
excludes: Creating plausible values when generation is requested.
Reconciling many heterogeneous sections and tables.

sample_tasks.instruction: Fully audit a nested candidate record against its supplied structural, scalar, array, and nullability constraints, then add one explicitly stated population value to the correct typed field.

Audit a property schema and map a narrative listing into its nested location, numeric, status, amenity, financing, and contact fields while retaining only supported facts and satisfying every constraint.

sections.name: Schema-Constrained Instance Generation
sections.outcome: Create plausible, internally coherent records that satisfy a supplied schema when values are not source-bound.
includes: Generating compatible scalar, array, object, and nullable values.
Maintaining cross-field plausibility while obeying strict constraints.
excludes: Presenting generated values as source-extracted facts.
Designing or modifying the supplied schema.

sample_tasks.instruction: Fully audit a nearly complete object against its nested types, enums, bounds, arrays, and nullability rules, then generate one missing bounded integer that keeps the object valid.

Generate a plausible highway record with constrained endpoints, junction arrays, concurrency sections, enums, nullable values, numeric bounds, and no undeclared properties after validating every applicable schema rule.

sections.name: Structured Format Serialization
sections.outcome: Serialize equivalent typed data accurately in hierarchical and tabular formats while preserving or explicitly reshaping its logical structure.
includes: Objects, arrays, scalars, nulls, repeated entities, special characters, and escaping.
Explicit flattening policies when a tabular format cannot preserve hierarchy directly.
excludes: Extracting unstated source facts.
Database import, transaction, or query execution.

sample_tasks.instruction: Serialize a two-field typed record as valid JSON.
Serialize one nested shipment dataset as JSON, YAML, and XML, then produce a parseable CSV projection of that same dataset using a stated flattening policy.

sections.name: JSON Serialization
sections.outcome: Represent nested typed records as syntactically correct JSON without changing their logical structure or scalar types.
includes: Objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, nulls, and JSON escaping.
Preserving required names and nesting.
excludes: YAML indentation and scalar-resolution rules.
XML elements, attributes, and CSV flattening.

sample_tasks.instruction: Serialize a record containing a string and integer as valid JSON.
Produce strict JSON for a deeply nested route record containing endpoint objects, junction arrays, escaped text, booleans, numbers, and null values without adding undeclared fields.

sections.name: YAML Serialization
sections.outcome: Represent nested typed records as unambiguous, parseable YAML with correct indentation, sequence structure, quoting, and scalar forms.
includes: Mappings, sequences, block and flow scalars, nulls, booleans, quoting, and indentation.
Quoting values whose plain forms would resolve to unintended types.
excludes: JSON-specific punctuation requirements.
XML markup and CSV flattening.

sample_tasks.instruction: Serialize a record containing a name and two-item list as correctly indented YAML.

Produce YAML for a nested deployment record containing multiline text, date-like strings, ambiguous boolean-like strings, arrays of objects, nulls, and punctuation while preserving every intended scalar type.

sections.name: XML Serialization
sections.outcome: Represent nested records and repeated entities as one well-formed XML document with the requested element and attribute structure.
includes: Single-root documents, elements, requested attributes, repeated records, namespaces when supplied, and escaping.
Mapping object and array structures into valid XML nesting.
excludes: DTD or XML Schema design unless requested.
HTML presentation markup.

sample_tasks.instruction: Serialize a name and publication date beneath one XML root element.
Create one well-formed XML report containing authors, funding records, nested metrics, repeated components, assessments, attributes requested by the structure, and correctly escaped text.

sections.name: CSV Flattening and Escaping
sections.outcome: Convert structured records into parseable CSV using an explicit, consistent policy for nested and repeated values.
includes: Headers, rows, delimiter quoting, embedded quotes, line breaks, and null representation.
Stable flattening or cell-serialization conventions for arrays and nested values.
excludes: Relational normalization into persistent tables.
Spreadsheet formulas, styling, or charts.

sample_tasks.instruction: Write a CSV header and one row whose text field contains a comma and quotation marks.
Flatten a nested chapter record containing arrays, booleans, punctuation-rich text, a multiline field, and repeated footnotes into parseable CSV with stable columns and a documented cell convention.

sections.name: Complex Document Integration
sections.outcome: Reconcile related facts from multiple prose sections and heterogeneous tables into a coherent nested collection of typed records.
includes: Entity resolution across sections and tables.
Preserving relationships among summary objects and repeated detail records.
excludes: Joining already loaded database tables with SQL.
Adding facts unsupported by the supplied material.

sample_tasks.instruction: Map every supported fact from a short prose summary into a constrained parent record, then reconcile one matching row from a supplied table into a new child array.
Map and validate a season overview, then reconcile its staff, rankings, standings, recruiting, and schedule tables into one nested dataset with consistent team identities and correctly typed values.

sections.name: Relational Databases
sections.outcome: Design, query, tune, modify, diagnose, migrate, and recover relational databases while preserving declared invariants.
includes: SQL retrieval, logical and physical design, execution plans, transactions, connectivity, migrations, and backup recovery.
Reasoning about constraints, indexes, generated statements, concurrency, and operational changes.
excludes: Document-store or graph-native modeling.
End-to-end orchestration of multi-system data pipelines.

sample_tasks.instruction: Define a table with a primary key and retrieve rows matching one condition.

For one subscription service, design and index its relational schema, answer a multistage SQL question, diagnose a slow plan and captured constraint failure, implement safe concurrent changes, and plan a reversible schema deployment with verified backup restoration.

sections.name: SQL Querying
sections.outcome: Write SQL that filters, relates, summarizes, composes, ranks, and recursively traverses relational data with correct row, null, duplicate, and grouping semantics.
includes: Single-table expressions, joins, grouped aggregation, subqueries, CTEs, set operations, windows, and recursive CTEs.
Deterministic ordering and deliberate duplicate handling.
excludes: DDL schema and index design.
Transaction boundaries and write-conflict handling.

sample_tasks.instruction: Select two columns from one table, filter by status, and order by timestamp.

Using one account hierarchy and its current and archived orders, write one query that recursively finds descendants, unions both order sources, joins payments, aggregates account totals, computes regional ranks and running totals, filters through a CTE, and returns deterministic results with stated null and duplicate behavior.

sections.name: Single-Table SQL Queries
sections.outcome: Retrieve and reshape rows from one table using precise projection, filtering, expression, null, distinctness, and ordering rules.
includes: SELECT expressions, aliases, predicates, sorting, limits, and scalar calculations.
Explicit null and duplicate handling.
excludes: Joins, grouped summaries, and recursive traversal.
Inserts, updates, and deletes.

sample_tasks.instruction: Select the name column from active rows in one table.
Return the latest twenty eligible products with computed discounted prices, explicit null handling, deduplication, and deterministic ordering.

sections.name: Relational Join Queries
sections.outcome: Combine related tables without unintended row loss, multiplication, or ambiguous matching.
includes: Inner, outer, semi, anti, and self joins.
Join cardinality, null-extension, and fan-out control.
excludes: Grouped aggregation as the central operation.
Physical join-algorithm or index tuning.

sample_tasks.instruction: Join orders to customers by customer identifier and return one field from each table.
Join customers, orders, optional payments, and product assignments while retaining unmatched customers, preventing assignment fan-out, and returning exactly one correctly matched row per order.

sections.name: Grouped SQL Aggregation
sections.outcome: Compute grouped summaries with correct null, duplicate, conditional, and group-filtering semantics.
includes: GROUP BY, aggregate functions, conditional measures, distinct aggregates, and HAVING.
Choosing denominators and counting null-bearing rows deliberately.
excludes: Joining multiple relations as the central challenge.
Windowed row-relative calculations.

sample_tasks.instruction: Count rows in each status group of one table.

From one transaction table, calculate per-region null-aware order counts, distinct-customer counts, conditional revenue, and average completed-order value, retaining only groups that meet a stated HAVING rule.

sections.name: Compositional SQL and Set Operations
sections.outcome: Structure multistage relational logic with subqueries, nonrecursive CTEs, and set operations while preserving intended duplicate semantics.
includes: Correlated and uncorrelated subqueries, reusable CTE stages, UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, and EXCEPT.
Making stage boundaries and deduplication auditable.
excludes: Recursive hierarchy traversal.
Window functions as the central operation.

sample_tasks.instruction: Use a subquery to retain products priced above the table's average price.

Combine current and archived eligibility records with the appropriate set operators, exclude blocked accounts through a correlated predicate, and organize the remaining business rules into named CTE stages.

sections.name: SQL Window Analytics
sections.outcome: Express row-relative analysis with partitioned ranking, navigation, framing, and running calculations without collapsing detail rows.
includes: ROW_NUMBER, rank variants, lag, lead, running totals, moving windows, and frame specifications.
Tie behavior and partition boundaries.
excludes: Recursive traversal.
Grouped aggregation when detail rows need not be retained.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a row number ordered by sale time within each customer.
For each account and month, retain monthly detail while calculating running revenue, prior-month change, a three-month moving average, and tied regional rank with explicit window frames.

sections.name: Recursive Relational Queries
sections.outcome: Use recursive SQL to traverse hierarchical or graph-like relational structures with explicit anchors, termination, depth, cycle, and path semantics.
includes: Recursive CTE anchors and steps, hierarchy expansion, path accumulation, and cycle prevention.
Depth limits and deterministic traversal results.
excludes: Nonrecursive CTEs used only for readability.
Graph-native query languages.

sample_tasks.instruction: Use a recursive CTE to return one category and all of its descendants to a fixed maximum depth.

Traverse an employee reporting hierarchy from a supplied manager, retain depth and path evidence, detect malformed cycles, stop at a stated bound, and return deterministic ancestor-to-descendant results.

sections.name: Relational Schema and Access Design
sections.outcome: Translate integrity and workload requirements into logical tables, indexes, and evidence-based query-performance improvements.
includes: Entities, relationships, keys, constraints, normalization, indexes, statistics, and execution plans.
Balancing integrity, read paths, and write costs.
excludes: Nonrelational aggregate or graph models.
Pipeline scheduling and operational alerting.

sample_tasks.instruction: Separate repeated customer details from orders and link the tables with a key.

For one subscription-billing workload, design normalized tables and constraints, choose a minimal index set, then inspect a supplied slow execution plan and revise the query or access paths without weakening integrity.

sections.name: Logical Schema and Database Constraints
sections.outcome: Model entities and relationships as normalized tables with suitable types, keys, and database-enforced invariants.
includes: Primary, foreign, unique, check, and nullability constraints.
Resolving repeating groups and update anomalies through normalization.
excludes: Pipeline acceptance gates and quarantine rules.
Diagnosis of a particular observed runtime violation.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose a primary key and add a foreign key between two simple tables.
Model products, suppliers, warehouses, inventory lots, and temporal supplier prices as normalized tables with cardinalities and database constraints that prevent invalid states.

sections.name: Index and Access-Path Design
sections.outcome: Choose relational indexes from concrete query, write, selectivity, and ordering requirements.
includes: Composite key order, covering, unique, and filtered indexes.
Write amplification and the access paths served by each index.
excludes: Diagnosing an observed execution-plan regression.
Changing logical facts solely to imitate an index.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose an index for equality lookup on a foreign key in a supplied schema.
Given a schema, query patterns, column selectivities, and write rates, propose a minimal index set and explain the predicates, joins, orderings, and coverage each index serves.

sections.name: Query Plan and Performance Diagnosis
sections.outcome: Interpret execution evidence to identify cardinality, access, join, memory, or statistics problems and select a justified query or database change.
includes: Estimated versus actual rows, scans, seeks, join algorithms, sorts, spills, statistics, and parameter sensitivity.
Comparing plans and runtimes before and after a change.
excludes: Index selection without an observed query or plan symptom.
Infrastructure tuning unrelated to database execution.

sample_tasks.instruction: Identify the plan operator responsible for a full-table scan and compare its estimated and actual row counts.

Diagnose a regressed reporting query from its SQL, actual plan, statistics age, parameter values, cardinality estimates, join choices, and spill evidence, then propose and evaluate the smallest justified rewrite, statistics, or index change.

sections.name: Reliable Relational Data Changes
sections.outcome: Apply multi-record changes atomically while preserving database invariants under failures, retries, and concurrency.
includes: Transactional mutations, idempotent requests, isolation, locking, optimistic versions, deadlocks, and retry boundaries.
Reasoning about rollback and invariant-preserving interleavings.
excludes: Read-only analytical querying.
Cross-system workflow compensation.

sample_tasks.instruction: Place two dependent updates in one transaction so either both persist or neither does.

Implement one inventory-reservation and payment-recording operation whose atomic writes, request deduplication, concurrent interleavings, deadlock handling, and retries preserve stock and payment invariants.

sections.name: Transactional Mutation
sections.outcome: Implement constraint-preserving multi-record mutations with atomic commit, rollback, affected-row checks, and idempotent request behavior.
includes: Ordered inserts, updates, deletes, and upserts within a transaction.
Rollback on failed preconditions and durable request keys.
excludes: Anomalies caused by competing transactions.
Cross-database atomicity.

sample_tasks.instruction: Insert an invoice and its first line item in one transaction.
Apply a batch of account transfers using guarded mutations, a durable request key, rollback on any invalid balance, and a result that distinguishes replay from a new transfer.

sections.name: Concurrency and Isolation
sections.outcome: Choose and implement concurrency controls that prevent specified anomalies while allowing acceptable parallelism.
includes: Isolation levels, locks, optimistic versions, serialization failures, deadlocks, and retries.
Constructing interleavings that demonstrate or rule out anomalies.
excludes: General distributed consensus across independent databases.
Performance tuning unrelated to concurrent correctness.

sample_tasks.instruction: Implement an atomic, rollback-safe, idempotent inventory reservation transaction, then add one optimistic version predicate so a concurrent stale writer is detected.

Implement transactional reservation and cancellation mutations, analyze their lost-update, write-skew, and deadlock interleavings, and select isolation, locking, versioning, and retry rules that preserve every stated invariant.

sections.name: Database Connectivity and Incident Diagnosis
sections.outcome: Establish database connectivity, capture executed commands, and trace observed integrity failures through application, schema, and concurrent behavior.
includes: Driver configuration, network and authentication checks, SQL logging, parameters, transactions, triggers, and constraint metadata.
Evidence-based isolation of the failing database operation.
excludes: Query optimization without an execution symptom.
Generic application debugging unrelated to database interaction.

sample_tasks.instruction: Identify the endpoint, database, authentication, and driver fields needed for a connection.

For one application incident, configure access to its custom database endpoint, capture the generated parameterized commands and transaction context, and diagnose the observed unique-constraint failure using runtime schema, trigger, mapping, and concurrency evidence.

sections.name: Driver and Connection Configuration
sections.outcome: Construct and troubleshoot database connection settings for a selected client, driver, endpoint, encryption mode, and authentication method.
includes: Provider syntax, host, port, instance, database, encryption, and credential mechanisms.
Separating client-format errors from DNS, routing, firewall, listener, and authentication failures.
excludes: SQL correctness after connection succeeds.
Embedding secrets in examples or source code.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a nondefault port to a database connection setting using the selected driver's syntax.

Configure a legacy application to connect through an installed driver to a remote database on a nonstandard port, then order checks that distinguish provider, DNS, routing, firewall, listener, encryption, and authentication failures.

sections.name: Executed-Statement Observability
sections.outcome: Capture database command text, bound parameters, timing, transaction context, correlation identity, and outcome without exposing sensitive values.
includes: Client logging, server tracing, query history, and operation correlation.
Distinguishing generated commands from pending in-memory changes.
excludes: Inferring commands from object state when direct capture is available.
Full application observability outside database calls.

sample_tasks.instruction: Enable command logging for one database context and capture a parameterized statement with its duration and outcome.

Design a diagnostic capture that correlates application operations with executed SQL, redacted parameters, transaction boundaries, durations, affected rows, and server errors across client and server evidence.

sections.name: Integrity Failure Diagnosis
sections.outcome: Explain an observed database constraint failure by tracing the executed change through runtime schema objects, implicit behavior, and concurrency.
includes: Unique, foreign-key, check, and null violations caused by direct statements, triggers, computed values, stale mappings, or races.
Comparing runtime metadata with application assumptions.
excludes: Defining pipeline quality gates.
Designing database constraints without an observed failure.

sample_tasks.instruction: Configure a complete capture of SQL text, parameters, timing, transaction context, correlation identity, and outcome for one failing insert, then identify the named constraint and conflicting key.

Capture and correlate a failing update, then diagnose its intermittent duplicate-key error by examining parameters, runtime index definitions, triggers, computed columns, identity mapping, transaction behavior, and concurrent changes.

sections.name: Database Change and Recovery Lifecycle
sections.outcome: Evolve database schemas safely and prove that database state can be restored to declared recovery objectives.
includes: Compatible migrations, data backfills, cutovers, rollback or roll-forward decisions, backups, restores, and recovery validation.
Coordinating application versions with database state.
excludes: Source-feed contract evolution outside the database.
Routine query and transaction implementation.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a nullable column in a migration and state how the old application version remains usable.

Plan one zero-downtime billing-schema release with expand-and-contract changes, resumable backfill, application cutover, pre-change backup, point-in-time restore drill, recovery objectives, and evidence for rollback or roll-forward.

sections.name: Relational Schema Migrations
sections.outcome: Plan and execute compatible, observable schema and data migrations across concurrently deployed application versions.
includes: Expand-and-contract changes, online DDL, resumable backfills, validation, cutover, and rollback or roll-forward.
Managing locks, defaults, and mixed-version compatibility.
excludes: Backup-media selection and restore drills.
External event-schema compatibility.

sample_tasks.instruction: Split adding a required field into a compatible nullable-add and later enforcement step.

Migrate a large orders table to a new customer key using online schema changes, chunked resumable backfill, dual-compatible application releases, validation, cutover, and explicit rollback or roll-forward criteria.

sections.name: Backup, Restore, and Database Recovery
sections.outcome: Design and validate backup and restoration procedures that meet stated data-loss and recovery-time objectives.
includes: Full and incremental backups, logs, point-in-time recovery, retention, encryption, restore ordering, and integrity checks.
Recovery drills and failover-versus-restore decisions.
excludes: Pipeline task replay.
Schema compatibility during application deployment.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose a backup interval that can meet a stated maximum data-loss objective.

Design backups and transaction-log retention for a critical database, restore it to a requested pre-incident point, validate consistency and application readiness, and demonstrate that the measured recovery meets its RPO and RTO.

sections.name: ETL and Data Pipelines
sections.outcome: Build repeatable pipelines that ingest changing sources, standardize and validate records, orchestrate recoverable execution, and deliver trustworthy analytical models.
includes: Batch and incremental ingestion, cleaning, linkage, quality gates, orchestration, monitoring, recovery, warehouse loading, and contract evolution.
Operational guarantees across repeated and partial executions.
excludes: One-off format conversion with no persistent flow.
Model training or downstream business interpretation.

sample_tasks.instruction: Define an extract, transform, and load sequence for one small source file and destination table.

Build one customer-order pipeline that combines an initial file snapshot with changes, standardizes and links records, enforces quality gates, evolves a source contract compatibly, loads an analytical model idempotently, and monitors and recovers partial runs.

sections.name: Data Ingestion
sections.outcome: Acquire bounded and changing source data while preserving provenance, identity, ordering, completeness, checkpoints, and replayability.
includes: Files, snapshots, APIs, change streams, source metadata, and ingestion boundaries.
Duplicates, late arrivals, malformed input, and incomplete delivery.
excludes: Business-rule transformation after acquisition.
Dashboard refresh and presentation.

sample_tasks.instruction: Read one delimited file and attach its source name and ingestion time to each record.

For one source system, ingest a complete partitioned snapshot and hand off to ordered change capture using manifests, provenance, duplicate detection, tombstones, atomic checkpoints, late-change handling, and safe replay.

sections.name: Batch Ingestion
sections.outcome: Load bounded files or snapshots completely and repeatably while retaining provenance and isolating malformed or duplicate input.
includes: File discovery, partition selection, parsing, manifests, source metadata, and completeness checks.
Atomic publication or quarantine of a bounded load.
excludes: Continuous change streams and offsets.
Downstream business transformations.

sample_tasks.instruction: Load one CSV file into typed records and retain its filename on each record.
Ingest a date-partitioned delivery of compressed files using a manifest, reject malformed rows, detect duplicate files and records, verify completeness, and publish the bounded batch atomically.

sections.name: Incremental and Change-Data Ingestion
sections.outcome: Capture new, changed, and deleted records incrementally with correct ordering, checkpoints, snapshot handoff, and replay semantics.
includes: High-water marks, log positions, change-data capture, tombstones, late changes, and atomic checkpointing.
Restarting without gaps or unintended duplication.
excludes: Bounded file completeness and manifest validation.
Applying business aggregations to captured changes.

sample_tasks.instruction: Fetch records newer than a stored high-water mark and advance that mark only after successful persistence.

Design a snapshot-to-change-stream handoff that applies inserts, updates, and deletes in order, persists offsets atomically with output, handles late events, and replays safely after consumer failure.

sections.name: Transformation and Data Quality
sections.outcome: Canonicalize heterogeneous values, resolve duplicate entities, and enforce measurable pipeline acceptance rules without hiding rejected or altered data.
includes: Value standardization, record linkage, survivorship, validation, quarantine, reconciliation, and provenance.
Separating repairs from quality observations.
excludes: Source transport and checkpoint management.
Database-enforced constraints for transactional invariants.

sample_tasks.instruction: Normalize two date formats into one typed date field and flag unparseable values.

Using one set of customer feeds, canonicalize names, addresses, dates, and units, link duplicate people with explicit evidence and survivorship rules, then apply field, relational, and aggregate acceptance gates with quarantine and reconciliation.

sections.name: Value Cleaning and Standardization
sections.outcome: Convert inconsistent field values into canonical typed representations using explicit, auditable transformation rules.
includes: Parsing, casing, whitespace, dates, units, categories, and missing-value policies.
Retaining original values and transformation provenance.
excludes: Cross-record identity resolution and survivorship.
Aggregate acceptance gates and reconciliation.

sample_tasks.instruction: Trim whitespace and normalize two textual date forms into one date type.
Standardize a product feed's names, identifiers, dates, decimal formats, currencies, units, categories, and missing-value markers while retaining original values and rule-level provenance.

sections.name: Record Linkage and Survivorship
sections.outcome: Identify records that refer to the same entity and construct a defensible surviving record from conflicting sources.
includes: Deterministic and fuzzy matching, blocking, match evidence, thresholds, clerical review, and survivorship.
Avoiding false merges and preserving lineage.
excludes: Within-field syntax standardization as the central operation.
Pipeline-wide completeness or reconciliation gates.

sample_tasks.instruction: Link two customer rows that share a normalized email address and retain both source identifiers.

Resolve overlapping customer feeds using blocking, exact and fuzzy evidence, explicit match thresholds, no-match and review outcomes, conflict-aware survivorship, and lineage to every contributing record.

sections.name: Pipeline Data Quality Controls
sections.outcome: Define and apply field, record, relational, and aggregate checks that make unacceptable pipeline data observable and actionable.
includes: Validity, completeness, uniqueness, reference checks, anomaly thresholds, quarantine, and reconciliation.
Quality metrics and acceptance gates for data products.
excludes: Database DDL constraints that protect transactional writes.
Diagnosis of a particular runtime database exception.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a required-field and allowed-range gate to supplied records and route failures to quarantine.

Create an order-load acceptance gate that checks schema validity, batch uniqueness, customer references, temporal consistency, amount reconciliation, anomaly thresholds, and accepted-versus-rejected counts.

sections.name: Pipeline Orchestration and Recovery
sections.outcome: Coordinate dependent pipeline stages so partitioned, repeated, and failed executions are scheduled, idempotent, observable, and recoverable.
includes: Dependencies, partitions, backfills, retries, stable keys, publication boundaries, metrics, alerts, and lineage-aware recovery.
Distinguishing task success from complete data-product readiness.
excludes: Field-specific transformation rules.
Database isolation inside one application transaction.

sample_tasks.instruction: Run a load task only after its extraction task succeeds.
For one partitioned daily pipeline, define dependency and backfill scheduling, idempotent publication, freshness and volume monitoring, and a lineage-scoped recovery from a partial upstream failure.

sections.name: Dependency and Partition Scheduling
sections.outcome: Express pipeline dependencies, schedules, readiness conditions, partition mappings, concurrency limits, and backfills.
includes: Directed acyclic task graphs, calendars, partition keys, readiness checks, and bounded parallelism.
Planning backfills across dependent partitions.
excludes: Duplicate-effect prevention during retries.
Failure diagnosis and recovery choice.

sample_tasks.instruction: Define a three-stage dependency order for extract, transform, and load tasks.
Schedule hourly events and daily reference data into regional daily outputs with readiness conditions, partition mappings, concurrency limits, and a dependency-correct backfill for a missed week.

sections.name: Idempotent Pipeline Execution
sections.outcome: Make repeated or resumed pipeline executions converge on the same target state without duplicate or conflicting effects.
includes: Stable run and record keys, staging, atomic replacement, merge semantics, and safe publication boundaries.
Handling partial output from prior attempts.
excludes: Business deduplication of genuinely distinct records.
Scheduling and alert threshold selection.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a stable source-record key so rerunning a load does not append duplicate target rows.
Design a partition load that stages output, merges by stable keys, publishes atomically, records completion state, and converges correctly after failures before, during, and after publication.

sections.name: Pipeline Monitoring and Alerting
sections.outcome: Measure data-pipeline health and delivery so failures and degradations are detected with actionable context.
includes: Freshness, volume, latency, error, and quality signals; structured logs; dashboards; and alerts.
Run, task, partition, and data-product readiness states.
excludes: Choosing replay, rollback, or recomputation procedures.
Infrastructure monitoring unrelated to data delivery.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a freshness metric and threshold alert to a daily load.

Define metrics, structured events, readiness states, dashboards, and deduplicated alerts for a partitioned pipeline whose failures may affect freshness, volume, latency, quality, or publication completeness.

sections.name: Pipeline Failure Recovery
sections.outcome: Diagnose failed or partial pipeline execution and restore the affected data scope without corrupting completed work.
includes: Lineage-aware impact analysis, safe retry boundaries, replay, rollback, and selective recomputation.
Post-recovery validation and incident scope.
excludes: Routine metric and alert design.
Blindly restarting jobs without locating the safe recovery boundary.

sample_tasks.instruction: Given one failed partition and a staging-only partial output, choose the safe partition retry boundary.

Diagnose a partial publication after an upstream partition failure, trace affected downstream products through lineage, choose among retry, replay, rollback, and selective recomputation, and specify validation before republishing.

sections.name: Analytical Modeling and Loading
sections.outcome: Shape transformed data into analytical models and load them while preserving grain, keys, history, late data, and reconciliation.
includes: Facts, dimensions, measures, surrogate keys, historical attributes, incremental merges, and corrections.
Declaring grain and source-to-target rules.
excludes: Operational schemas optimized for transactional writes.
Visualization and interpretation of resulting metrics.

sample_tasks.instruction: Separate one event measure from its descriptive entity attributes into a fact and dimension.

For one sales dataset, design facts and conformed dimensions with declared grains and history rules, then incrementally load changes, late events, and corrections while resolving keys and reconciling measures.

sections.name: Dimensional Modeling
sections.outcome: Design fact and dimension tables whose grain, keys, measures, and historical behavior support specified analytical questions.
includes: Transaction, periodic snapshot, and accumulating snapshot facts; conformed dimensions; and slowly changing attributes.
Additivity, role-playing dimensions, and explicit grain.
excludes: Physical dashboard layouts.
Normalized operational design without an analytical workload.

sample_tasks.instruction: Declare the grain of a purchase-line fact and identify its customer and product dimensions.
Model orders, shipments, returns, and inventory snapshots with conformed dimensions, appropriate fact types, additive measures, role-playing dates, and historical customer segments.

sections.name: Incremental Warehouse Loading
sections.outcome: Load supplied analytical facts and dimensions incrementally while preserving surrogate-key resolution, history, corrections, and source reconciliation.
includes: Slowly changing dimension application, early and late facts, merges, correction handling, and audit totals.
Ordering dimension and fact loads.
excludes: Designing source-capture protocols.
Choosing the dimensional model itself as the central operation.

sample_tasks.instruction: Resolve one incoming business key to a dimension surrogate key before inserting a fact.

Load a supplied star model from a change batch by applying historical dimension updates, assigning surrogate keys, handling early and late facts, correcting prior rows, and reconciling source counts and measures.

sections.name: Data Contract and Pipeline Schema Evolution
sections.outcome: Evolve source and target data contracts without silently dropping, misinterpreting, or corrupting data across mixed producer and consumer versions.
includes: Additive and breaking changes, defaults, versioning, compatibility checks, drift detection, dual reads or writes, and backfills.
Coordinating contract rollout across pipeline stages.
excludes: Relational DDL migration mechanics inside one database.
Routine invalid-record checks under an unchanged contract.

sample_tasks.instruction: Classify adding an optional source field and specify how an older consumer should handle it.

Evolve an order-event contract through a field rename and type change using versioned schemas, producer and consumer compatibility gates, drift alerts, dual-read rollout, historical backfill, cutover, and rollback criteria.

sections.name: NoSQL, Graph, and Distributed Data Systems
sections.outcome: Design document, key-value, wide-column, and graph models and choose distributed placement and consistency behavior from workload requirements.
includes: Aggregate and graph modeling, native access paths, partitioning, replication, read guarantees, and distributed write coordination.
Explicit denormalization, duplication, and failure semantics.
excludes: Using a nonrelational store solely as an interchangeable relational database.
Search or vector retrieval without a relevant data-model requirement.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose between embedding a small object and storing it as a separately addressed record for one read pattern.

Design one global social-messaging service using document profiles, key-value preferences, wide-column message timelines, and a relationship graph, then specify physical partitions, replica topology, read guarantees, and invariant-preserving cross-record writes.

sections.name: Document, Key-Value, and Wide-Column Modeling
sections.outcome: Model denormalized aggregates and key-addressed records around concrete read, write, growth, ordering, and retention patterns.
includes: Embedding and references, key composition, bounded partitions, clustering order, and controlled duplication.
Update, fan-out, and storage consequences of materialized access paths.
excludes: Physical replica placement and failover topology.
Graph traversal as the primary access pattern.

sample_tasks.instruction: Model one user preference as a directly addressable key and structured value.

For one messaging workload, model conversation metadata as documents, preferences as direct key-value records, and time-ordered messages as bounded wide-column rows supporting inbox, conversation, pagination, retention, and unread access patterns.

sections.name: Document Data Modeling
sections.outcome: Define document aggregates, embedding boundaries, references, identities, and update rules that serve specified access patterns.
includes: Nested objects and arrays, schema variation, document-level atomicity, bounded growth, and controlled duplication.
Embedding-versus-reference decisions.
excludes: Opaque key-only values.
Multi-hop graph traversal.

sample_tasks.instruction: Embed a small shipping address in an order document that is always read with that order.

Model articles, authors, revisions, comments, and tags as documents, choosing embedding or references for each relationship while accounting for growth, atomic updates, duplication, and required queries.

sections.name: Key-Value Data Modeling
sections.outcome: Design stable keys and values for direct lookup, conditional update, expiration, and simple secondary access requirements.
includes: Key namespaces, composite lookup keys, value structure, TTLs, compare-and-set behavior, and controlled duplicated keys.
Predictable point access.
excludes: Ordered range scans within wide-column partitions.
Physical sharding, rebalancing, and replica placement.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose a key that retrieves one customer's preferences directly.

Design key-value records for sessions, user preferences, feature assignments, and idempotency tokens with namespaces, TTLs, conditional updates, value versions, and any explicitly justified duplicate lookup keys.

sections.name: Wide-Column Access-Path Modeling
sections.outcome: Design logical partition keys, clustering order, buckets, and materialized tables for predictable range and query-specific access.
includes: Bounded logical partitions, clustering columns, time buckets, sparse attributes, and duplicated access tables.
Write fan-out and retention per logical table.
excludes: Physical shard placement, online rebalancing, and replica topology.
Direct opaque-value lookup as the only access pattern.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose a logical partition key and clustering timestamp for one device's daily readings.

Design query-specific wide-column tables for device readings and regional alerts with bounded logical partitions, clustering order, time buckets, retention, pagination, sparse fields, and explicit write fan-out.

sections.name: Graph Data Modeling and Querying
sections.outcome: Represent relationship-rich domains as graphs and express bounded paths, neighborhoods, and aggregates over the resulting model.
includes: Node and edge identities, labels, direction, properties, constraints, indexed starts, and traversal semantics.
Cycle, path-length, duplicate, and cardinality control.
excludes: Physical partition and replication policy.
Using graph storage for records with no relationship-driven query.

sample_tasks.instruction: Represent two people and their directed employment relationships to one organization as nodes and edges.

Using one fraud-investigation domain, model accounts, devices, transactions, merchants, and shared identifiers, then query bounded suspicious paths with cycle control, retained path evidence, endpoint aggregation, and deterministic ranking.

sections.name: Graph Schema Modeling
sections.outcome: Choose nodes, edges, direction, properties, labels, identities, and constraints that preserve relationship semantics.
includes: Promoting relationships or attributes to first-class entities when identity or history matters.
Cardinality, temporal edges, uniqueness, and indexed starting points.
excludes: Complex traversal implementation.
Document embedding without graph queries.

sample_tasks.instruction: Model customers and products with a directed purchased edge carrying a timestamp.

Design a temporal supply-chain graph with organizations, facilities, products, shipments, ownership, and certifications, including identity rules, edge direction, properties, cardinalities, constraints, and indexed entry points.

sections.name: Graph Traversal Queries
sections.outcome: Write queries over a supplied graph model that return intended paths, neighborhoods, or aggregates with explicit direction, bounds, and duplicate semantics.
includes: Pattern matching, variable-length traversal, shortest paths, cycle control, path predicates, aggregation, and projection.
Selecting indexed starting nodes from the supplied model.
excludes: Redesigning the graph schema.
Unbounded exploration with unspecified termination.

sample_tasks.instruction: Query all products reached by one outgoing purchased edge from a specified customer in a supplied graph.

Query bounded paths linking two accounts through shared devices or payment instruments, exclude repeated nodes, retain path evidence, aggregate risk by endpoint, and return deterministic ranked results.

sections.name: Distributed Data Placement and Consistency
sections.outcome: Choose physical partitioning, replica topology, read guarantees, and distributed write mechanisms that meet scale, locality, availability, and invariant requirements.
includes: Shard keys, rebalancing, replica placement, failover, consistency levels, conflict handling, and multi-record coordination.
Behavior during lag, network partitions, retries, and ambiguous outcomes.
excludes: Logical document or wide-column access-path design.
Infrastructure provisioning unrelated to data semantics.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose a physical shard key that distributes bounded tenant records while retaining tenant-local access.

For one multi-region commerce dataset, choose physical shards and rebalancing, place replicas for regional failures, define read guarantees for profiles and orders, and coordinate inventory and balance writes through lag, partitions, retries, and failover.

sections.name: Physical Data Partitioning and Rebalancing
sections.outcome: Distribute records across physical shards to balance load, preserve useful locality, bound skew, and support online growth.
includes: Hash and range partitioning, composite shard keys, hotspots, query fan-out, and online resharding.
Estimating placement and movement consequences.
excludes: Logical wide-column table and clustering design.
Replica placement and failover topology.

sample_tasks.instruction: Select a physical shard key that spreads tenant records while retaining tenant-local reads.
Partition a high-volume event store by tenant and time, quantify skew and query fan-out, mitigate hot shards, define split thresholds, and plan online rebalancing as tenants and traffic grow.

sections.name: Replica Placement and Failover Topology
sections.outcome: Place and promote replicas to meet locality, durability, availability, and failure-domain requirements.
includes: Regional and zonal placement, leaders and followers, synchronous and asynchronous replication, failover, and rebuild behavior.
Capacity and lag implications of topology choices.
excludes: Selecting logical or physical partition keys.
Application-visible read consistency beyond what topology can support.

sample_tasks.instruction: Place three replicas across failure zones so one zone loss does not remove every copy.

Design a multi-region replica topology for an order store, specifying leader placement, synchronous and asynchronous links, read locality, regional failover, promotion safety, rebuild capacity, and behavior during replica lag.

sections.name: Replicated Read Consistency
sections.outcome: Select and implement read guarantees that match stated freshness, session, ordering, latency, and availability requirements.
includes: Strong, bounded-staleness, causal, monotonic-read, read-your-writes, and eventual guarantees.
Leader, quorum, session-token, and lag behavior.
excludes: Atomic multi-record write coordination.
Shard-key and replica-placement design.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose a read-your-writes mechanism so a user immediately observes a successful profile update.

Specify read guarantees and routing for profiles, timelines, permissions, and order status during replica lag and regional failover, identifying which reads require strong, causal, session, bounded-stale, or eventual behavior.

sections.name: Distributed Transactions and Conflict Handling
sections.outcome: Preserve named cross-record or cross-partition invariants through concurrency, retries, conflicts, partial failure, and ambiguous outcomes.
includes: Atomic distributed transactions, conditional writes, consensus-backed commits, sagas, idempotency, conflict detection, and deterministic resolution.
Explaining aborts, retries, and uncertain commit results.
excludes: Read-only consistency selection.
Partition-key and replica-topology design.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add an idempotency key and conditional version check to one cross-partition transfer so a retried request cannot apply twice.

Design write coordination for replicated balances and inventory across partitions, preserving declared invariants through concurrent updates, partial commits, regional partitions, retries, conflict resolution, and ambiguous client outcomes.
